svg.title: Legendre incidence and transported coefficients
svg.desc: The real N equals two slice maps the point t equals one quarter, x equals one half and covectors tau equals one, xi equals y to the hyperplane s equals one quarter plus y over two, sigma equals one and eta equals minus one half. The parameter y runs from minus one to one. Extension by zero and derived open image, both shifted by N, are inverse projective kernels. Finite Hom transports to the actual transformed coefficient module. Identification with a target cutoff is an additional module comparison.
svg.text: Legendre incidence and transported coefficients
Exact open-image choice · input antipode · strict action on the coefficient object
1. The inverse projective kernels
K = j! CΩ [N] L = transpose(Rj* CΩ) [N]
K ∘ L ≃ CΔX L ∘ K ≃ CΔY
The two shifts add to [2N], the real affine-fibre dimension.
Off the diagonal: compact cohomology of the derived puncture image is zero.
Actual compact fibres and coherent inverse maps: LIT.1–LIT.6.
2. A point conormal becomes a hyperplane conormal
τ = 1, ξ = y; s = t + xy, σ = 1, η = −x.
Real slice: t₀ = 1/4, x₀ = 1/2, −1 ≤ y ≤ 1.
x
t
y
s
Point fibre; covectors (ξ,τ) = (y,1)
Base: s = 1/4 + y/2
Normal covector (η,σ) = (−1/2,1)
σ ds + η dy = τ dt + ξ dx. All complex phases occur. LIT.8–LIT.9, LIT.28.
3. Retain the actual coefficient module
Φ HomR(P,GY) ≃ HomR(P,ΦR GY)
P is bounded finite free; every differential and homotopy is retained.
ĜX = ρ* ΦR GY
ĜX ⇢ GX : an additional module-derived comparison
A coefficient ring isomorphism alone does not identify these two objects.
Hom is a vector complex; its coefficients need not commute.
Strict coefficient transport and finite Hom: LIT.18–LIT.24, LIT.29–LIT.30.
